turns.en: Good morning, how are you feeling today? How did you sleep? Any pain overnight?
turns.cy: Bore da — sut dach chi'n teimlo heddiw? Sut wnaethoch chi gysgu? Unrhyw boen dros nos?
chunks: 'any' → unrhyw in the free-choice question (S9); poen feminine, so boen (R8)

turns.en: Not bad at all. The pain's nearly gone - just a twinge when I turn over.
turns.cy: Ddim yn ddrwg o gwbl. Mae'r boen bron wedi mynd — dim ond gwayw pan dw i'n troi drosodd.
chunks: the wedi-perfect with bron before it, where English puts 'nearly' before the participle too
just a twinge when I turn over
dim ond gwayw pan dw i'n troi drosodd
restrictive 'just' → dim ond; the indefinite article erases inside it

turns.en: Excellent - and your chest sounds much better too. Let's get that scan done this morning and aim for home tomorrow.
turns.cy: Ardderchog — ac mae'ch brest chi'n swnio lot yn well hefyd. Dewch i ni gael y sgan yna wedi'i neud bore 'ma, ac anelu am adra fory.
chunks: and your chest sounds much better too
ac mae'ch brest chi'n swnio lot yn well hefyd
Let's get that scan done this morning
Dewch i ni gael y sgan yna wedi'i neud bore 'ma
English's causative 'get X done' relocates to cael X wedi'i neud — the wedi-passive under cael

turns.en: Tomorrow. Right. I'll believe it when I see the taxi.
turns.cy: Fory. Reit. Mi gredaf i pan wela i'r tacsi.
chunks: I'll believe it when I see the taxi
Mi gredaf i pan wela i'r tacsi
English's object 'it' erases — credu stands alone; the when-clause takes the Welsh future, where English uses a present

turns.en: Fair enough! If today's scan is clear and you stay this well overnight, then tomorrow it is.
turns.cy: Digon teg! Os ydy sgan heddiw'n glir ac os arhoswch chi mor dda â hyn dros nos, fory amdani.
chunks: Welsh puts digon before the adjective, where English puts 'enough' after
If today's scan is clear and you stay this well overnight
Os ydy sgan heddiw'n glir ac os arhoswch chi mor dda â hyn dros nos
the os must be restated on the second limb, and 'this well' takes the comparative frame mor … â hyn
the X amdani ratifier (R3) — and 'then' disappears into it entirely

turns.en: That's the best news I've had all week.
turns.cy: Dyna'r newyddion gorau dw i wedi'u cael drwy'r wythnos.
chunks: That's the best news I've had all week
Dyna'r newyddion gorau dw i wedi'u cael drwy'r wythnos
newyddion is plural in Welsh, so the resumptive is 'u, not 'i

turns.en: Good morning, how are you feeling? Any pain overnight?
turns.cy: Bore da — sut dach chi'n teimlo? Unrhyw boen dros nos?
chunks: distinct from 'how are you feeling TODAY' → …heddiw

turns.en: When exactly can I go home, doctor? I've been in a week now.
turns.cy: Pryd yn union ga i fynd adra, doctor? Dw i i mewn ers wythnos rŵan.
chunks: When exactly can I go home, doctor?
Pryd yn union ga i fynd adra, doctor?
the permission ga i, not the ability fedra i — it is leave he wants, not strength
I've been in a week now
Dw i i mewn ers wythnos rŵan

turns.en: I hear you - a week is plenty. If today's scan is clear and you stay this well overnight, then tomorrow. I won't promise what I can't be sure of, but that's the honest plan.
turns.cy: Dw i'n eich clywed chi — mae wythnos yn hen ddigon. Os ydy sgan heddiw'n glir ac os arhoswch chi mor dda â hyn dros nos, yna fory. Wna i ddim gaddo be fedra i ddim bod yn siŵr ohono fo, ond dyna'r cynllun gonest.
chunks: English's bare 'plenty' takes the Welsh intensifier hen, which has no English reflex here
If today's scan is clear and you stay this well overnight, then tomorrow
Os ydy sgan heddiw'n glir ac os arhoswch chi mor dda â hyn dros nos, yna fory
'then' here is the apodosis marker yna, its fourth distinct role in the walk (S1)
I won't promise what I can't be sure of
Wna i ddim gaddo be fedra i ddim bod yn siŵr ohono fo
English strands 'of'; Welsh must conjugate it as ohono fo

turns.en: Tomorrow, all being well. I'll settle for that.
turns.cy: Fory, os bydd bob dim yn iawn. Mi setla i am hynny.
chunks: Fory, os bydd bob dim yn iawn
English's absolute participle relocates to a full os-clause in the future

turns.en: Let's get the scan done this morning and take it from there. I'll come back to you myself with the result.
turns.cy: Dewch i ni gael y sgan wedi'i neud bore 'ma, ac mi gymrwn ni hi o fan'na. Mi ddo i'n ôl atoch chi fy hun efo'r canlyniad.
chunks: Let's get the scan done this morning
Dewch i ni gael y sgan wedi'i neud bore 'ma
ac mi gymrwn ni hi o fan'na
feminine hi for the situation — English's 'it' is genderless
I'll come back to you myself with the result
Mi ddo i'n ôl atoch chi fy hun efo'r canlyniad
motion toward a person takes at, conjugated as atoch chi (§4)

turns.en: Thank you, doctor. That's all I wanted - an honest answer.
turns.cy: Diolch, doctor. Dyna'r cwbl ro'n i isio — ateb gonest.
chunks: the indefinite article erases; gonest soft-mutates after the masculine noun in this appositive

turns.en: Good morning, how are you feeling today? Any pain overnight?
turns.cy: Bore da — sut dach chi'n teimlo heddiw? Unrhyw boen dros nos?

turns.en: The pain's back, actually. Worse than yesterday, if anything.
turns.cy: Mae'r boen yn ôl, a deud y gwir. Gwaeth na ddoe, os rhywbeth.
chunks: Mae'r boen yn ôl, a deud y gwir
⚠ line — 'if anything' → os rhywbeth, the same rhywbeth as the offers (S9)

turns.en: That's important - I'm glad you've told me. Show me exactly where, and I'll examine you properly now rather than guessing.
turns.cy: Mae hynna'n bwysig — dw i'n falch eich bod chi wedi deud wrtha i. Dangoswch i mi'n union lle, ac mi wna i'ch archwilio chi'n iawn rŵan yn hytrach na dyfalu.
chunks: dw i'n falch eich bod chi wedi deud wrtha i
⚠ line — the eich bod chi that-clause; 'tell' governs wrth
and I'll examine you properly now rather than guessing
ac mi wna i'ch archwilio chi'n iawn rŵan yn hytrach na dyfalu

turns.en: Just here, doctor - and it woke me at four. It's different from before. Sharper.
turns.cy: Yn union fan'ma, doctor — ac mi wnaeth hi fy neffro i am bedwar. Mae hi'n wahanol i o'r blaen. Yn finiocach.
chunks: ⚠ line — precise 'just', so yn union, not the erasing softener
and it woke me at four
ac mi wnaeth hi fy neffro i am bedwar
⚠ line — feminine hi for the pain (R8)
Mae hi'n wahanol i o'r blaen
⚠ line — Welsh's 'different' governs i, not the from-preposition English uses
⚠ line — the synthetic comparative with its obligatory predicative yn

turns.en: Here's what happens next: I'll examine you now, we'll take some bloods, and I'll come back to you myself before lunch with a plan. You won't be left wondering.
turns.cy: Dyma be sy'n digwydd nesa: mi wna i'ch archwilio chi rŵan, mi gymrwn ni waed, ac mi ddo i'n ôl atoch chi fy hun cyn cinio efo cynllun. Chewch chi mo'ch gadael yn pendroni.
chunks: mi wna i'ch archwilio chi rŵan
⚠ line — English's clinical plural 'bloods' erases; gwaed is a mass noun
and I'll come back to you myself before lunch with a plan
ac mi ddo i'n ôl atoch chi fy hun cyn cinio efo cynllun
⚠ line — the promise the whole scene turns on
Chewch chi mo'ch gadael yn pendroni
⚠ line — Welsh's cael-passive in its negative, with the mo contraction

turns.en: Before lunch. Thank you, doctor. That's all I wanted - to know what's happening.
turns.cy: Cyn cinio. Diolch, doctor. Dyna'r cwbl ro'n i isio — gwybod be sy'n digwydd.
chunks: ⚠ line — gwybod for factual knowing (S5); the sy'-focus free relative
